BiblicalUsage: Chomets is vinegar, the sour wine, and it appears in the law, the proverbs, the psalms and the story of Ruth. The Nazarite must separate from vinegar, the sluggard is as vinegar to the teeth, the psalmist is given vinegar to drink in his thirst, and Boaz tells Ruth to dip her morsel in the vinegar.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe vinegar in these verses is sourness itself, and the psalmist drinking it is the picture of Christ on the cross. I hold that Ruth dipping her morsel in vinegar shows God's kindness reaching even into the sour things of life.
